newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank to issue statement shortly - spokeswoman.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank to issue statement shortly - spokeswoman.

text.p: A spokeswoman for the Bundesbank said on Thursday that the central bank expected to issue a statement shortly.
The spokeswoman did not give ay details about the subject matter of the expected statement.
In an slightly unusual move, Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday flew into Frankfurt by helicopter at around 1000 GMT to attend the Bundesbank's council meeting.
German finance ministry officials are allowed to attend Bundesbank regular fortnightly council meetings but do not have the right to vote.
Earlier, sources from the country's coalition government had said Waigel would attend the meeting to discuss the revaluation of the country's gold reserves.
The sources said Waigel was not considering selling the reserves.

The finance ministry also said earlier that 1997 tax estimates showed an 18 billion mark shortfall, sparking speculation that the government may be seeking to revalue the central bank's assets in a bid to bring debt levels down to qualify for European monetary union (EMU).
Waigel was seen leaving the Bundesbank at around 1235 GMT, but, did not speak to reporters waiting outside the entrance to the Bundesbank grounds.
